rationale: Apply one consistent platform boundary across the Harrison Street–1547 data-center program. Direct manager, co-sponsor, seller, SEC and current operator evidence shows that Wells, Pittock, Orangeburg, Cheyenne and South Bend are constituent facilities or asset SPVs inside one continuing national data-center and connectivity platform. None of the separate property, borrower, lease or project LLCs establishes a distinct manager-level operating company, and no subsequent sale of any of the five target facilities was identified through August 30, 2026. Retire all five duplicate standalone company records into the existing Harrison Street–1547 Data Center & Connectivity Platform, preserve their names and legal SPVs as aliases, retain the platform's separate Harrison Street and FifteenFortySeven owner periods, and do not infer a Harrison Street fund, vehicle, ownership percentage or ownership of corporate 1547.

companyFieldUpdates.description: Harrison Street–1547 Data Center & Connectivity Platform is the manager-level U.S. program through which Harrison Street and FifteenFortySeven Critical Systems Realty invest in and operate carrier hotels, colocation facilities and connectivity-focused data centers. The countable platform is a recurring multi-asset investment and operating program rather than one asserted umbrella legal entity; corporate 1547 is the operator and co-sponsor, not a company shown to be owned by Harrison Street. Wells was the first joint acquisition in 2020, Pittock followed in early 2021, Orangeburg and Cheyenne were included in the November 2021 four-asset portfolio acquisition, and South Bend was added in 2024. Separate title-holding, borrower, lease and project LLCs remain asset-level vehicles beneath the platform. Harrison Street's exact fund or managed account, both parties' ownership percentages and the private cap tables of individual SPVs are not publicly disclosed. Current operator and transaction sources show the five facilities continuing in the program, with no later sale identified through August 30, 2026.

set.event: Harrison Street and 1547 completed their first joint acquisition, the Wells Building carrier hotel and data center in Milwaukee, beginning the disclosed multi-site platform.
1547 and Harrison Street acquired Portland's Pittock Block carrier hotel and added the 302,200-square-foot facility and its dense network ecosystem to their connectivity-focused platform.

CIM Group sold Midway/CHIL1, CHIL2, Orangeburg/ORNY1 and Wyoming/Cheyenne/CHWY1 to the Harrison Street–1547 joint venture in a four-asset acquisition that followed the parties' earlier Wells Building acquisition, expanding the relationship to six data centers while 1547 remained manager.

The partners added Union Station/SBIN1 in South Bend to the connectivity portfolio in September and AlohaNAP in October, when they described the joint national platform as exceeding one million square feet.

Harrison Street and 1547 announced full occupancy and further expansion at Orangeburg/ORNY1, a 232,000-square-foot facility on a 23-acre campus with 24 MW of provisioned power, confirming continuing joint platform activity.

milestoneTransfers.event: Pittock Block added 302,200 square feet, 179 service providers, and one of the Northwest's two primary internet exchanges to the 1547-Harrison Street platform.
The buyers disclosed planned capacity and facility upgrades following the Union Station/South Bend acquisition.
The Cheyenne data center was fully leased to a national virtual infrastructure and IT services customer when 1547 and Harrison Street acquired the portfolio.
